mechanism: A {{check}} strategy that evaluates constraints in a declared {{hierarchy}}, cheapest first (e.g., existence -> {{validate}} (schema) -> {{understand}} (semantics), which is also increasing abstraction in the common case). It uses a {{sequence}} of {{gate}}s where lower-level failures halt execution immediately, preventing resource waste on higher-level checks for fundamentally broken inputs.
invariants: A lower layer's failure stops the {{sequence}}; the next layer does not run.
Layers run in their declared order, cheapest first.
Each layer declares whether a finding is a failure or a warning.
failure_modes: Misordered layers: an expensive check sits below a cheap one, so the halt saves nothing.
Warning inflation: findings are classed as warnings to keep the {{sequence}} running, which defeats the halt.
